clue.text: Show Aberdeen duo used goods store

indicators.note: letters that have been used are worn and knocked about, so the three words are rearranged

parts.note: these three words supply exactly the fifteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A Scottish pair use a warehouse to stage a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Show' looks like the start of the definition or a verb, but it is part of the fodder; the definition is only the last two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonded warehouse is a secure depot where imported goods are kept before duty is paid on them.

clue.text: Reps plied oil giant with drink

explanation.definitionFit: An espresso is a strong coffee, a kind of drink.

parts.note: tarps (tarpaulins) are waterproof sheets

explanation.definitionFit: The sprat is a small silvery sea fish of the herring family.

clue.text: Is ballet out of place in revolutionary venue?

parts.note: the two words provide the eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Asks whether a ballet would be inappropriate at a venue for revolutionaries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' hints at an anagram, but here it belongs to the definition: the prison stormed in the French Revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bastille, the Paris fortress-prison stormed in 1789, is the iconic site of the French Revolution.

definitions.note: read as 'escort is': the 's joins definition to wordplay

parts.note: a gig is a live music performance
lo is an old word meaning look or see

explanation.surface: An escort's act turns out to be nothing worth watching.
explanation.definitionFit: A gigolo is a man paid to accompany or be the lover of a woman, a male escort.

clue.text: Tree feller from the north's got backbone

parts.note: a Scot is a fellow from the north of Britain; the 's stands for 'has'
the spine is the backbone

explanation.surface: A northern lumberjack is shown to have courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tree feller' looks like a lumberjack, but the definition is just 'Tree' and 'feller' is a folksy fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scots pine is a common conifer native to northern Europe and the Highlands.

clue.text: America dropping A-bombs on old war zone

indicators.note: bombs is read as a verb: the remaining letters go off and land jumbled
dropping a letter means leaving it out of the word

parts.note: the country's name supplies the starting letters
the A of A-bombs is the letter taken out

explanation.surface: The United States drops atom bombs on a former battlefield.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A-bombs' reads as atomic bombs, but it splits: the letter A is dropped and 'bombs' signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: The Crimean peninsula was the scene of the Crimean War of the 1850s, so it is a historic battleground.

parts.note: a community is a society of people
a charge is an attack, as in a cavalry charge

explanation.surface: Society turns on a tax that was meant to be popular.
explanation.walkthrough: The community charge was Britain's hated 1990 poll tax, so 'popular' is ironic: it was a levy on the people, not one they liked.
explanation.definitionFit: The community charge was a flat-rate local tax paid by every adult, a levy on the populace.

clue.text: Hopi and Osage working on parts of canal?

indicators.note: working suggests the letters being worked over and reshaped

parts.note: the Hopi people's name gives four of the letters
the Osage people's name gives the other five

explanation.surface: Two Native American peoples labour on stretches of a canal.
explanation.walkthrough: The canal is the alimentary canal, not a waterway; the question mark flags this.
explanation.definitionFit: The gullets are sections of the digestive tract, which anatomists call the alimentary canal.

indicators.note: drivers reversing their car fits the surface, and tells us to read the letters backwards

parts.note: the RAC (Royal Automobile Club) is a British motoring organisation for drivers
go means energy or eagerness, as in 'full of go'

explanation.surface: Delivery drivers eagerly back up with their freight.
explanation.definitionFit: Cargo is goods carried by ship, plane or lorry, which is what freight means.

indicators.note: the outer word hangs around the inner one, enclosing it

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe
Sandhurst is home of the Royal Military Academy, the British Army's officer college

explanation.surface: Someone at an army academy is told not to loiter idly.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dormant is asleep or not active for now, like a volcano that has not erupted for years.

clue.text: Ideal work for model and single mother

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
the Model T was the famous Ford car
I is the Roman numeral one
mum is British for mother

explanation.surface: A perfect job for a model who is also a single mother.
explanation.definitionFit: The optimum is the best possible condition, the ideal one.

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the long signal in Morse code, written as a line

explanation.walkthrough: Inspector Morse had style, but the second sense is the code's long signal, beside the dot.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means stylish verve and also the long mark of Morse code, two unrelated senses of one word.

clue.text: Riverside flats of old design and dull

indicators.note: the letters are given a new design, a fresh arrangement

parts.note: these two short words give the five letters to rearrange
plain means unadorned or dull

explanation.surface: Apartments by the river built to an old-fashioned, plain design.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flats' looks like apartments, but it means level ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A floodplain is the low level land beside a river that is covered when it overflows.

clue.text: Lawyers as yet confused about rent

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go about, around, the other piece
confused letters are mixed up, so the two words are rearranged

parts.note: these two words give the five letters to rearrange
rent is the past tense of rend, so torn

explanation.surface: Legal advisers are still unclear about the rent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like money owed to a landlord, but it is the verb rend, to tear.
explanation.definitionFit: Attorneys are lawyers, particularly in American usage.

clue.text: Preacher and the PA stole away

indicators.note: taken as gone astray, so the letters wander out of order

parts.note: these words give the seven letters to rearrange; 'and the' just links

explanation.surface: A preacher and his personal assistant made off with something.
explanation.walkthrough: PA here is just two letters of the fodder, not the personal assistant of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostle is a missionary who spreads the faith, so a preacher.

clue.text: Section of the mosque are into polo

indicators.note: one word goes into another, placed inside it

parts.note: Polo is a brand of mint with a hole in the middle
the word itself goes in whole, as written

explanation.surface: Members of a mosque turn out to be keen on polo.
explanation.walkthrough: Polo is not the sport but the British ring-shaped peppermint sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: A minaret is the slender tower of a mosque, from which the call to prayer is made.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: noon, the sun at its highest
second meaning: a great circle on the globe running through the poles

explanation.walkthrough: The Circle line is a London Underground route, but here it is a line of longitude on the globe.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means noon and also the north-south great circle used to measure longitude.

clue.text: Reportedly took cycle left on the verge

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said aloud, so we take a word with the same sound

parts.note: a cyclist rode the bike
left is a side, as opposed to right

explanation.surface: Someone apparently cycled off along the grass edge.
explanation.definitionFit: The roadside is the strip at the edge of a road, the British verge.

clue.text: Exaggerated story by Rome lunatic about headless horseman

indicators.note: the jumbled letters sit about the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: these two words give the six letters to rearrange

indicators.note: headless means the first letter is cut off

parts.note: a rider is a horseman

explanation.surface: A tall tale out of Rome about the Headless Horseman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' looks like a link word but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Embroidery figuratively means decorative exaggeration added to a tale.

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts

parts.note: the little word itself, flipped over in the down light

explanation.surface: Students with degrees stand to take part in an election.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballot is a secret vote, or the process of voting.

explanation.walkthrough: 'Refrain' sounds like a song's chorus, apt for a singer, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To desist is to stop or hold back from doing something, the verb refrain.

explanation.definitionFit: Talc, or talcum powder, is a soft mineral powder.

parts.note: a tiger, the big cat

explanation.surface: An animal can be heard in the woods of the north.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech the big cat sounds just like the forest word.
explanation.definitionFit: The taiga is the swampy coniferous forest belt of subarctic Siberia and North America.

definitions.note: playful: an adjective standing in for the plural noun, things that are shapes

parts.note: OB is old boy, a former pupil; the 's is a link
longs are long trousers

explanation.surface: A former pupil's trousers are well-fitting.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is loose: these are shapes, not shapely.
explanation.definitionFit: Oblongs are rectangles longer than they are wide, geometric figures.

parts.note: plumb means exactly, as dead does in 'dead centre'
the main is a poetic word for the open sea

explanation.surface: A plumber installs a main pipe for a garden water feature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Water feature' suggests a garden fountain; it is a geographic one.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dead Sea is a salt lake between Israel and Jordan, a natural body of water.

explanation.walkthrough: Read as a hairy hound's naughty story, the clue gives the long rambling joke with a pointless punchline.
